User: obviously it has to be first-class for that app's codebase, right?

Assistant: Right — and that's the sharper, correct way to put it. NMP's repo must *not* know about your kind 232123. But the **machinery** that turns "a kind schema" into a fully-typed, generated, drift-gated builder has to be a reusable seam the app can point at its *own* schema — so that inside the app's codebase, kind 232123 is exactly as first-class as kind:1 is inside NMP: typed Rust builder, generated Swift/Kotlin/TS bindings, its own contract/drift gate, riding the generic sign/route pipeline. Anything less and "apps can make up kinds" degrades to "apps can hand-roll an ActionModule and FFI shim," which isn't the same promise. [...] User: publish a gh issue to explore this question and design space, make it clear that the intent goal is what I stated -- an app should easily be able to define its made up kind with its schema builder and whatnot and should be a first-class citizen. Don't add your commentary on how to do this

Assistant: On it. Let me check the available labels, then file a clean design-exploration issue that leads with your stated goal and the factual current-state evidence — no solution commentary.

Assistant: Filed: **[#2408 — App-defined event kinds should be first-class citizens](https://github.com/pablof7z/nostr-multi-platform/issues/2408)**

It leads with your goal stated plainly — an app should easily define its own made-up kind (number, schema, builder) and have it be a first-class citizen in the app's own codebase, on par with NMP's built-in kinds, with no upstreaming, no hand-rolling NMP-generated boilerplate, and no raw/untyped fallback. Below that it captures the factual current-state evidence (with file:line) and frames the design space as open problem-questions only.
